name: Hale
epithet: Keeps the inn on the tarn at Coldmere
appearance: A big, easy man going soft at the middle, bald on top with grey curls round the edges, in a clean apron, with a broad, open face of the kind a whole valley trusts with its news. He keeps a fat account book open on the end of his bar, a ribbon in it and a pencil in its spine.
portrait_alt: Portrait of Hale: a big, round-faced older man, bald on top with grey curls round the edges, smiling warmly, in a clean white apron over a dark waistcoat and a linen shirt, with a fire burning and pewter tankards on the shelves of the inn behind him.
last_seen_doing: Had his book open at Rae's elbow while the coat was sold, and turned a page.
now: At the end of his bar with the book open.

quote.text: We'll talk the summer's loads in the morning, Rae.

known_facts.fact: He keeps a fat account book open on the end of his bar and wrote the cart and its company into it.
He gave the company the inn's loft, with nobody else in it that night.
known_facts.evidence: Nobody in it. Nobody will be, tonight.

relationships.label: her uncle
relationships.note: He keeps the inn on the tarn; he paid for her cart and oxen once, and she has been paying him back by the load.
